name: Roadwarden's Sword
description: A plain, sharp steel sword with a brown leather grip and a scabbard patched at the throat. Made for years of ordinary road work.

name: Riveted Basket Sword
description: A straight sword with a protective basket of crossed steel strips. Its balance rewards a controlled hand rather than a broad swing.

name: Whitepass Arming Sword
description: A mountain-made sword with a short, sturdy guard and a grip that remains secure through winter gloves. The fuller bears a small maker's goat.

name: Lanternedge
availability: Enchanted weapon shops; old expedition equipment
description: A pale sword whose narrow fuller shines like a covered lantern when its pommel is turned. A sliding brass shutter dims the light for travel.

name: Common Cavalry Saber
description: A slightly curved steel saber with a simple knucklebow. The scabbard carries the dents of practical manufacture rather than a distinguished campaign.

name: Copperleaf Cutlass
description: A broad cutlass with copper leaves embossed on its guard. Sailors favor its short reach on crowded decks and its easy-to-clean fittings.

name: Snowchain Saber
description: A robust saber with a cord loop at the grip and a fur-lined scabbard mouth. Freight escorts use it on exposed mountain routes.

name: Emberglass Smile
description: A dark saber threaded with amber-red glass. After a flame working, tiny sparks travel along the enclosed channels like insects returning to a hive.

name: Plain Dueling Rapier
description: A slender steel rapier with a modest swept hilt. Its tip is sharp, its finish plain, and its maker has spent the money on the temper.

name: Blue-Ribbon Rapier
description: A lively rapier with a narrow cyan ribbon tied beneath the guard. The ribbon can be replaced; the careful balance is the reason to buy it.

name: Three-Ring Estoc
description: A stiff thrusting sword with three steel rings protecting the hand. Its maker has left a neat mark inside the guard where only its owner sees it.

name: Last Word at Supper
description: A silver-finished rapier that gives one delicate dinner-bell note when drawn. The blade is quite real despite its owner's opportunity for an entrance.

name: Traveler's Greatsword
description: A long, sharp sword meant for two hands, with plain fittings and a broad cloth shoulder sling. It is workmanlike rather than ceremonial.

name: Hearthforged Greatsword
description: A broad two-handed sword with a dark central ridge and a heat-colored guard. Its weight sits close enough to the hands for deliberate recovery.

name: Avalanche Cleaver
description: A thick-backed greatsword with a squared tip and a deeply textured grip. Mountain mercenaries use its weight without pretending it is light.

name: The Red Horizon
availability: Exceptional recovered armory; major specialist collection
description: A colossal two-handed sword of dark red steel, its blade marked with a thin gold line from heel to tip. It appears in old descriptions of a battle whose victor was never recorded.

name: Working Dagger
description: A sturdy pointed dagger in a plain belt sheath. The rough spine offers a thumb purchase for careful work.

name: Sleeveguard Dirk
description: A long dagger with a secure hand guard and a narrow sheath. Duelists carry it for the space a larger weapon cannot comfortably cover.

name: Black Thread Stiletto
description: A slim triangular dagger with matte fittings and a tightly retained sheath. It draws without the clatter of loose metal.

name: The Apologetic Knife
description: A black dagger that murmurs a little bell-like apology whenever its point clears the sheath. Nobody has found a quieter way to draw it.

name: Matched Street Blades
description: Two short steel blades in a paired belt rig, fitted to be used together. The simple guards leave room for a close, mobile fighting style.

name: Copperfin Pair
description: A matched pair of short curved swords with fish-tail pommels. Their scabbards nest together without rattling.

name: Rimehook Twins
description: Two hooked short blades with heavy guards and winter-wrapped grips. They favor close control over long lunges.

name: Quarrelsome Sisters
description: A pair of dark swords, one etched with a sun and the other with rain. Touching their pommels produces two different, distinctly argumentative notes.

name: Ashwood Spear
description: A straight ash shaft carrying a leaf-shaped steel head. A leather sleeve marks the point where its balance rests.

name: Ferrywatch Spear
description: A ferryman's long spear with a short crossbar below its point. The butt is capped for purchase on slippery boards.

name: Goatstep Boar Spear
description: A broad hunting spear with a reinforced shaft and stout lugs. Its fittings are easy to replace far from a forge.

name: Rootwake Lance
description: A long spear with living-looking root patterns under a smooth amber finish. Its shaft gives a soft green glimmer when resting against healthy soil.

name: Gatekeeper's Halberd
description: A steel axe blade, hook and spear point mounted on a long square-cut shaft. Its reach makes it awkward company in a narrow room.

name: Freightyard Billhook
description: A sturdy hooked polearm built for controlling a close approach. The head is secured with two long reinforcing strips.

name: Silverstep Glaive
description: A long curved blade carried on a carefully tapered shaft. Silver wire at the grip records its balance points.

name: Windward Procession
description: A sweeping glaive with fine holes through its blade. Moving it in a practiced arc produces a low, clean chord and stirs the loose ribbons at its heel.

name: Woodcutter's Fighting Axe
description: A short, sharp axe with a reliable hickory haft and a head light enough for fighting. Its edge still handles ordinary camp work.

name: Notched Caravan Axe
description: A compact broad axe with a protective steel strip down the front of its haft. A small notch in the heel fits its travel cover.

name: Cairn-Splitter Axe
description: A heavy single-bit axe with a flared edge and a rough black haft. It is built for hard, committed blows.

name: Widow's Promise
description: A beautiful black axe with a white silk grip. Old repairs hold their shape poorly around it, and healers tend to move it away before beginning work.

name: Ironheaded Maul
description: A two-handed wooden haft carrying a plain iron head. The leather grip is thick enough to replace after a wet season.

name: Quarryman's Hammer
description: A compact war hammer with a reinforced haft and a narrow back spike. Its maker began as a quarry toolwright.

name: Thunderhead Sledge
description: A broad two-handed hammer with a dark steel face and a cord-wrapped lower grip. Every fitting is oversized and reassuringly plain.

name: The Uninvited Knock
description: A war maul with a polished brass striking face shaped like an expressionless door knocker. Its impact makes a deep, resonant report even against soft timber.

name: Plain Flanged Mace
description: A short steel mace with six blunt flanges and a leather wrist loop. The head has no decorative sharp edges to catch in its cover.

name: Whitepass Morningstar
description: A compact spiked mace with a strong winter grip. A fitted wooden cap protects everything else in the owner's pack.

name: Pilgrim's Iron Cudgel
description: An iron-shod hardwood club with a carved grip worn smooth by years of use. Its ornamental cord carries several repaired knots.

name: Bellringer's Courtesy
description: A hollow-headed mace whose internal tongue can be secured for travel. Unfastened, it lends a clear toll to a deliberately placed strike.

name: Yew Hunting Bow
description: A straightforward wooden bow with a waxed string and a simple leather grip. Arrows are carried separately.

name: Horn-Backed Recurve
description: A short recurve strengthened with horn and sinew. Its padded travel cover matters as much as its handsome finish.

name: Pinefold Longbow
description: A tall, patient bow made from seasoned mountain wood. The pale grip bears tiny marks used to check its string alignment.

name: The Far Green Silence
description: A longbow of translucent green wood with no visible maker's seam. A drawn string leaves the surrounding air peculiarly still until released.

name: Stockman's Crossbow
description: A plain wooden crossbow with an iron prod and a sturdy loading stirrup. Bolts are bought and carried separately.

name: Compact Lever Crossbow
description: A short crossbow with a folding lever for deliberate reloading. Its mechanism is accessible beneath a latched side plate.

name: Watchtower Arbalest
description: A heavy crossbow with a deeply braced stock and a slow, positive winding mechanism. It rewards choosing a position before the fight starts.

name: Clockwork Sparrow
description: A brass-trimmed crossbow whose little mechanical bird clicks when its ordinary bolt track is seated correctly. It is exacting about maintenance.

name: Ironshod Quarterstaff
description: A tough wooden fighting staff with iron caps and a plain central grip. Its strength comes from wood and sound construction.

name: Weighted Traveling Staff
description: A staff whose concealed internal weights give its ends a firm, predictable swing. A threaded cap allows repairs.

name: Ambercore Battlestaff
description: A durable fighting staff with a thin mana-bearing amber core. Its reinforced ends are intended for actual staff work.

name: The Rain-Hating Staff
description: A pale battlestaff whose upper cap unfolds into a broad waxed canopy. It drips collected rain with an indignant ticking sound.

name: Short Iron Chain
description: A short length of well-linked chain with reinforced hand loops. Using it carelessly is an excellent way to strike one's own knuckles.

name: Weighted Chainblade
description: A short blade joined to a balanced weight by a measured chain. Each end has a fitted travel restraint.

name: Twin-Hook Chain
description: A paired set of hooked blades joined by a robust chain, intended for a practiced two-handed method. A padded case keeps it civilized in transit.

name: Firefly Catenary
description: A dark chain weapon whose insulated grips frame fine yellow sparks beneath the link enamel. The sparks gather along its length during lightning workings.

name: Braided Fighting Whip
description: A weighted braided whip with a reinforced handle and a replaceable end. Its coiled cover is plain, thick leather.

name: Ribbonsteel Lash
description: A flexible lash reinforced with thin steel segments. It takes careful maintenance to keep the joints moving smoothly.

name: Barbed Silk Whip
description: A dark braided whip with short, deliberately spaced metal barbs. Its owner's gloves should be sturdier than its elegant handle suggests.

name: Violet Reprimand
description: A violet lash with silver stitching and a faint scent of cold flowers. The stitching brightens under a deliberately channeled enchantment.

name: Balanced Twinblade
description: Two short blades share a central grip wrapped for both hands. Its long travel case is as conspicuous as the weapon.

name: Brassguard Twinblade
description: A double-ended weapon with protective flared guards near its central grip. Brass grip bands make alignment easy to feel.

name: Snowwheel Twinblade
description: A compact twinblade with narrow blades and winterproof grip wrapping. A broad scabbard encloses both ends together.

name: The Blue Hour's Argument
description: A double-ended silver weapon whose opposing blades carry different blue reflections under the same light. Its grip bears an inscription worn beyond legibility.

name: Reinforced Fighting Gloves
description: Thick leather gloves with rigid knuckle plates and reinforced seams. They are meant for trained punches rather than delicate repairs.

name: Brassknuckle Wraps
description: A fitted pair of fighting wraps built around small brass knuckle guards. The palm remains flexible for grappling.

name: Stonebrace Gauntlets
description: Heavy articulated gauntlets with broad wrist supports. Small gaps at the joints keep a tightly closed fist from pinching.

name: Laughing Giant's Gloves
description: Oversized fighting gloves of enchanted hide. Their palms are surprisingly dexterous, but the weight is very noticeable during a nimble scramble.

name: Ironbound Round Shield
description: A wooden round shield with an iron rim and boss. A padded inner strap keeps the edge from battering the forearm.

name: Caravan Kite Shield
description: A long shield with a reinforced lower point and a faded trade-road pattern. Its repair-friendly construction suits repeated travel.

name: Riveted Tower Shield
description: A broad shield with a padded shoulder rest and a deep viewing notch. Its owner pays for the protection in carried weight.

name: The Door That Refused
description: An immense shield paneled like an old painted door, complete with a useless little brass knocker. Its hinges are ornamental; its weight is not.

name: Steel-Ribbed War Fan
description: A folding fan with blunt steel ribs and a secure central pin. Closed, it is a compact striking tool; open, it is unmistakably a weapon.

name: Painted Crane Fans
description: A matched pair of reinforced fans painted with red cranes. Their weighted ribs suit practiced turns as well as formal performance.

name: Mirrorleaf Battle Fan
description: A broad fan with polished metal leaves and a reinforced thumb rest. A cloth sheath protects the reflective finish.

name: Curtain Call in Gold
description: A gold-leafed war fan whose painted audience changes expressions as its folds move. The tiny figures never leave the painted stage.

name: Long-Haft War Scythe
description: A purpose-made fighting scythe with a straighter blade mounting than a farm tool. Its long haft demands two hands and room to turn.

name: Hooked Harvest Glaive
description: A long curved blade with an inward hook, fitted on a steel-braced wooden haft. Its removable cover is very carefully labeled.

name: Blackfield Reaper
description: A dark two-handed scythe with a stiff haft and a narrow crescent blade. Its maker has favored fighting balance over ornament.

name: The Undertaker's Compliment
description: A silver-gray war scythe with small bone-colored ceramic beads hanging beneath its blade. The beads give a low chord near an active spiritual working.

name: Padded Traveling Cap
description: A close-fitting quilted cap with ear flaps that tie beneath the chin. It packs flat and dries beside a modest fire.

name: Plain Steel Helm
description: An open-faced steel helmet with a replaceable padded liner. The brow is deliberately free of decorative projections.

name: Caravan Sallet
description: A low steel helmet with a broad, carefully placed viewing opening. Its long rear protects the neck without a cumbersome collar.

name: Glassworker's Hood
description: A thick hood with a clear hinged face screen and a soft internal band. Soot wipes easily from its smooth surface.

name: Pinefold Hunting Hood
description: A lined green hood with a weathered outer surface and discreet loops for local foliage. Its heavy hem stays down in a crosswind.

name: Star-Pinned Scholar's Hat
description: A soft pointed hat whose small silver star is actually a neatly caged mana crystal. Its brim can be buttoned out of the wearer's eyes.

name: Stormreader's Goggles
description: Brass goggles with adjustable blue lenses that make fine electrical traces easier to distinguish. Old scratches remain visible in the left lens.

name: Ashen Diadem
description: A black metal circlet warm at the temples. Its red stones brighten around flames while medicinal enchantments feel unusually stubborn nearby.

name: The Crown of Small Complaints
description: A thin silver crown ornamented with tiny closed mouths. In quiet rooms its wearer hears indistinct muttering, usually about matters of astonishing triviality.

name: Quilted Field Coat
description: A tough padded coat with a slit hem and broad inner pockets. The stitching is plain, close and easy to repair.

name: Leather Brigandine
description: A leather outer coat carrying small steel plates beneath its lining. Its buckles can be worked with cold fingers.

name: Plain Mail Shirt
description: A long steel mail shirt with leather bindings at the neck and sleeves. A padded underlayer makes its weight much more agreeable.

name: Rivet-and-Rime Cuirass
description: A carefully fitted steel breastplate with fur-backed straps and brass rivets. Mountain armorers leave room for a practical winter layer.

name: Surveyor's Long Vest
description: A sturdy sleeveless field vest with numbered specimen pockets and a narrow waterproof notebook sleeve. Its shoulders are reinforced for carrying straps.

name: Rainleaf Caster's Coat
description: A dark green coat whose treated cloth beads rain into tidy lines. Fine blue stitching follows the cuffs and shoulder seams.

name: Mirror-Sewn Robe
description: A flowing robe with tiny polished discs hidden in its hems. As its wearer moves, the cloth catches slightly misplaced glints of light.

name: Glassheart Cuirass
description: A clear crystal breastplate fitted around a milky central stone. Its cool pressure makes the wearer feel strangely fragile beneath the formidable shell.

name: Emberrest Mantle-Coat
description: A thick red traveling coat with charcoal-black seams. Its lining keeps a comfortable warmth long after the wearer leaves the hearth.

name: The Quiet Citadel
description: A dark cuirass made from interlocking plates finer than ordinary smiths can reliably reproduce. Its tiny joints close with a sound like a distant latch.

name: Hardwearing Field Trousers
description: Stout trousers with patched knees and a gusseted seat. Their owner can kneel on rough ground without immediately regretting it.

name: Leather Greaves
description: Boiled-leather leg guards lined with felt. The straps are broad enough to distribute pressure during a long walk.

name: Articulated Steel Greaves
description: Steel knee and shin guards with overlapping joints. A small maker's mark identifies the left piece when they are laid out for cleaning.

name: Climber's Split Skirt
description: A reinforced divided overskirt with secure ties and a narrow inner pocket. The hem stays out of a climber's knee bend.

name: Woolridge Winter Leggings
description: Heavy wool leggings with a close windproof outer weave. Replaceable straps keep them from riding above a winter boot.

name: Duelist's Silver Seams
description: Close-fitting dark trousers traced with flexible silver stitching at the knees and hips. They are much less delicate than their formal appearance suggests.

name: Rootbound Chausses
description: Soft mail leggings whose green fastenings resemble tightly closed buds. Soil caught in the weave falls free with a firm shake.

name: The Heavy Road
description: Dark traveling leggings with strangely dense hems. Their wearer can sustain a burden for longer but quickly notices the weight when trying to leap.

name: Leather Road Boots
description: High leather boots with replaceable laces and sound soles. Their appearance improves considerably after a brush and a little oil.

name: Hobnailed Working Boots
description: Thick boots with iron hobnails and reinforced toes. On polished floors they announce their owner well before the conversation starts.

name: Whitepass Snow Boots
description: Fur-lined boots with deep tread and leather covers over the lacing. The removable felt liners dry overnight near a hearth.

name: Quietstep Soft Boots
description: Soft-soled boots with carefully padded seams and no loose fittings. The leather is dull rather than artificially black.

name: Iron-Toed Duel Boots
description: Balanced leather boots with small steel toe caps and close ankle supports. Their soles turn predictably on a clean practice floor.

name: Ladderkeeper's Boots
description: Work boots with firm arches and a squared heel that rests securely on a rung. The maker has reinforced every point touched by a climbing strap.

name: Cloudtread Slippers
description: Pale slippers woven with soft sky-fiber. Their soles briefly display tiny cloud shapes after each step on a cold surface.

name: Moss-Mannered Boots
description: Brown boots with living-looking moss tucked beneath their laces. The little green fronds curl inward when the boots are polished.

name: The Impatient Heels
description: Elegant boots whose heels tap a brisk rhythm when their wearer stands still. Performers argue whether the habit is charming or infuriating.

name: Gravelfall Sabatons
description: Steel foot guards with dark violet stones set inside the ankle joints. Their weight seems to settle evenly over whatever surface bears them.

name: Plain Work Gloves
description: A practical pair of thick leather gloves with replaceable palms. Fine needlework is possible, but not pleasant.

name: Supple Archery Gloves
description: Close-fitting gloves with smooth fingers and a reinforced drawing hand. Their seams are kept away from a bowstring.

name: Riveted Winter Gauntlets
description: Articulated gauntlets with warm liners and oversized strap ends. A mitten cover can be pulled over them between fights.

name: Alchemist's Waxed Gloves
description: Close gloves with a treated outer surface and long cuffs. Their stitching is easy to inspect for the damage a careless experiment leaves behind.

name: Fine Mechanist's Gloves
description: Thin work gloves with grippy fingertips and small removable steel bracers. Their owner can feel a loose screw through the palm.

name: Mercywork Gloves
description: Cream-colored gloves stitched with delicate red thread. The fingers retain their sensitivity even after repeated washing.

name: Touch of the Distant Forge
description: Black gloves with copper seams that glow faintly while metal is being worked. Their fingertips smell of warm iron even after cleaning.

name: Thorn-Bitten Gloves
description: Green gloves whose fine seams occasionally press like tiny thorns. A dry rose is embroidered across each palm.

name: Plain Wool Cloak
description: A heavy wool cloak with a reliable wooden clasp. It does what a traveler expects and makes no claims beyond that.

name: Waxed Rain Cape
description: A broad cape of waxed cloth with a deep hood. Rain gathers in its folded hem if the wearer forgets to shake it out.

name: Snowchain Freight Cloak
description: A thick cloak cut short enough to clear pack straps and haul lines. A red lining makes it visible in bad mountain weather.

name: Greenblind Shoulder Cape
description: A mottled shoulder cape with a hood that breaks up the outline of the face. Its colors suit woodland rather than every conceivable background.

name: Keeper's Tool Mantle
description: A reinforced mantle with narrow loops for a few carefully fastened tools. Its weight lies across the shoulders instead of pulling at the neck.

name: Night-Lantern Cloak
description: A dark cloak dotted with small luminous threads inside the hood. The wearer can cover or expose them by turning its edge.

name: Borrowed Breeze Cape
description: A light cape whose corners seem perpetually interested in the nearest breeze. Its clasp is a tiny pair of folded brass wings.

name: The Cloak That Sulks
description: A charcoal cloak that draws itself into unflattering folds when displayed for admiration. In a quiet corner it hangs perfectly.

name: Hearth Away From Home
description: A heavy red travel cloak with a soft amber lining. Even in an unfamiliar shelter, it carries a faint scent of dry wood and clean wool.

name: Copper Grip Ring
description: A thick copper ring with a rough inner ridge. Porters turn the ridge toward the palm before taking a difficult grip.

name: Brass Scholar's Ring
description: A plain brass ring carrying a tiny hinged lens. The lens folds out neatly over a page or small fitting.

name: Amber Spark Ring
description: A warm amber chip sits in a copper band. A narrow gold seam makes the stone look as though it contains one small ember.

name: Rainmark Ring
description: A silver band carrying a blue stone with a persistent waterline across its middle. The line shifts when the ring is turned.

name: Pebble-Crowned Ring
description: A simple iron ring set with an unpolished gray pebble. Fine pale veins circle it like miniature strata.

name: Tumbling Feather Ring
description: A small feather is suspended within a clear setting. It turns lazily whenever a fresh breeze reaches the ring.

name: Storm-Nail Ring
description: A dark steel ring with a single yellow inclusion. When rubbed clean, its surface briefly smells of a summer storm.

name: Thawglass Ring
description: A clear blue ring cold enough to mist in warm air. Its interior looks cracked, though the smooth stone has no loose edge.

name: Sunpin Ring
description: A gold setting frames a tiny pale crystal. The crystal holds the last color of daylight for several minutes after sunset.

name: The Crooked Halo
description: A slightly tilted golden ring that looks straight only from an unflattering angle. Its pale radiance makes a practiced innocent expression difficult to sustain.

name: The Ring That Applauds
description: A silver ring etched with tiny hands. When tapped twice against a hard surface it answers with a brief, rather enthusiastic patter.

name: The Patient Orbit
description: A violet stone moves slowly around this open ring without touching its metal. Its orbit remains stubbornly unchanged by the wearer's attempts to hurry it.

name: Wooden Road Pendant
description: A small carved road marker on a sturdy cord. The back is flat enough to write a name and an address.

name: Iron Needle Pendant
description: A short iron needle hangs inside an open silver frame. It takes a controlled metallic working to turn it precisely without contact.

name: Greenhouse Heart
description: A clear pendant holding a tiny living sprig. It needs an occasional drop of clean water and resents being left in a hot drawer.

name: Bronze Listener
description: A hollow bronze bead hangs on a short chain. Humming near it produces a warm vibration under the fingers.

name: Mercyseed Locket
description: A white ceramic locket with space for a small pressed leaf or personal note. Its polished surface warms in a healer's hand.

name: Open-Circle Medallion
description: A silver circle interrupted by one deliberate gap. Tiny ceramic figures have been worked into the edge, all facing outward.

name: Glass Moth Pendant
description: A blue glass moth with thin silver antennae. Its wing patterns appear different in a reflection, though the glass itself never moves.

name: Three-Question Amulet
description: Three small colored stones are set beneath a hinged cover. Old diviners polish one stone before each difficult question.

name: Black-Salt Charm
description: A black crystal sealed in a narrow silver cage. Loose dust gathers around its frame in sharp, orderly lines.

name: Ferryman's Copper
description: A weathered copper disc on a dark cord, stamped with an empty little boat. Its surface gives a faint note when brushed during a spiritual working.

name: Glutton's Clasp
description: A heavy pendant shaped like a smiling open mouth. Its wearer feels brimming with magical capacity and unreasonably tired after climbing stairs.

name: The Smallest North
description: A silver compass pendant whose needle circles a point just outside its case. Its maker's diagram is engraved so finely that magnification is needed to read it.

name: First-Shift Brooch
description: A little brass shopfront pin with a replaceable name strip. The clasp is stronger than its cheerful appearance suggests.

name: Quiet Courtesy Pin
description: A small silver pin finished so smoothly that it never catches a formal sleeve. Its shape resembles a carefully folded greeting card.

name: Tailor's Little Moon
description: A crescent-shaped brooch engraved with tiny stitch marks. Its curved backing rests flat against a lined collar.

name: Ruby Field Pin
description: A practical ruby-red marker pin with a strong double clasp. Mapmakers use its shape as a reference when sketching a position.

name: The Modest Peacock
description: A splendid peacock brooch whose metal feathers fold inward when someone tries to spread them. It looks most dignified when left alone.

name: Jester's Honest Face
description: A tiny enamel mask changes from a grin to an embarrassed frown when turned upside down. Its owner tends to become a little too expressive.

name: Pressed-Fern Brooch
description: A real fern has been sealed between two clear plates. Small scratches in the silver frame suggest long use in a working conservatory.

name: The Listening Widow
description: A silver spider brooch whose slender legs vibrate with nearby sound. It makes surrounding details easy to notice and remarkably difficult to disregard.

name: Kitchen Laureate's Pin
description: A small golden spoon crossed with a flowering sprig. The stem smells faintly of warm citrus after it is polished.

name: The Empty Audience
description: A black enamel theater pin with seats too tiny to count easily. When warmed in the hand, it carries the distant hush just before a performance begins.

name: Plain Load Belt
description: A broad leather belt with a dependable brass buckle. Its back is padded where a heavy strap tends to rub.

name: Climber's Waist Strap
description: A stout belt with reinforced attachment loops and a buckle that can be checked by touch. It suits careful use with actual climbing equipment.

name: Quick-Pocket Belt
description: A close-fitting belt with shallow secured pockets. Its owner can kneel or roll without loose contents banging together.

name: Field Medic's Belt
description: A cleanable belt with labeled loops for actual medical supplies. Its empty pouches are conspicuous after a busy day's work.

name: Seven-Notch Gunmetal Belt
description: A gray belt with a heavy reinforced buckle and broad waist support. Seven small scratches mark an old adjustment point.

name: The Breath Between Hills
description: A supple green belt that smells of rain on grass. Its buckle is carved as a traveler resting against a milestone.

name: Pilgrim's Comfortable Burden
description: A broad belt with two small polished stones sealed inside its lining. The stones pull at the waist during a jump but settle pleasantly during a long walk.

name: Coincounter's Belt
description: A leather belt with a small mechanical counting wheel beside its purse loop. The wheel clicks to zero when the buckle is opened.

name: Lucky Button Cord
description: A bright assortment of buttons on a braided cord. Someone has sewn a smiling face onto the least valuable one.

name: Surveyor's Marker Charm
description: A flat enamel marker with a numbered rotating disc. The back has a narrow groove for a pencil rubbing.

name: Rosewater Knot
description: A neatly tied ribbon charm around a tiny reusable scent bead. Its little stopper is secured by a very fine chain.

name: Companion's Paw Token
description: A smooth wooden token shaped like a resting paw. Chew marks suggest that an earlier owner tested its durability thoroughly.

name: The Patient Pawn
description: A small weighted chess pawn on a short chain. Its base is broad enough to stand on a map without falling over.

name: Root-and-Rivet Token
description: A wooden charm held together with visible brass rivets. A tiny shoot follows the joining seam without splitting the wood.

name: Moonlit Mortar Charm
description: A pale stone charm shaped like a miniature mortar. Its bowl darkens when stained and lightens again after a careful cleaning.

name: Second Thought Talisman
description: A blue stone carved into a small open hand. It is soothing to hold and lends a decidedly hesitant air to a dramatic threat.

name: The Unfinished Equation
description: A metal tag engraved with a geometric proof that stops just before its final line. Its blank lower edge is polished by worried thumbs.

name: Bellwind Promise Cord
description: A braided cord carrying a soft wooden bell. Its tongue can be tied still before approaching a nervous creature.

name: The Unpaid Tab
description: A bronze tavern token whose tally lines rearrange whenever it is polished. Bartenders often take an immediate dislike to it.

name: Grave-Courtesy Beads
description: A strand of gray ceramic beads with one empty place in the sequence. Their soft clicking is often used to keep a spiritual working measured.

name: Birch Practice Wand
description: A short mana-bearing birch wand with a plain linen grip. Its light weight suits careful introductory control.

name: Amber-Nib Wand
description: A slender wand ending in a protected amber nib. Its owner can trace a familiar pattern with very little pressure.

name: Bronze Conductor's Baton
description: A polished baton weighted at the heel, with a bronze ring around its tip. Its hollow handle gives a clear reference note.

name: Rootglass Casting Wand
description: A green glass wand enclosing a fine branching root. The root is visible from every angle and has never grown beyond its original outline.

name: Folded-Lecture Grimoire
description: A compact grimoire with foldout geometric plates and a tough mana-bearing binding. Blank leaves remain for its owner's corrections.

name: Cloudfield Observation Atlas
description: A waterproof field atlas with ruled pages for cloud forms, distances and weather signs. Its maps cover established routes rather than every island.

name: Bone-Handled Medical Lancet
description: A small, carefully sharpened medical instrument in a lined case. The bone handle has enough texture to grip with wet fingers.

name: Coppercoil Focus
description: An insulated hand focus containing a neatly wound copper coil. Small inspection windows expose the state of its fittings.

name: Portable Mana Gauge
description: A sturdy dial instrument for comparing local magical activity. Its reading needs interpretation and a checked reference point.

name: Folding Brass Astrolabe
description: A small astrolabe with nested rings and an unusually clear horizon scale. Its leather case is covered in old alignment marks.

name: Surveyor's North Compass
description: A dependable magnetic compass with a simple sighting notch. Nearby metal can make its useful little needle thoroughly unhelpful.

name: Folding Map Board
description: A light wooden board with brass clamps and a foldout rule. It provides a flat writing surface on a very uncooperative rock.

name: Reusable Field Snare Set
description: A small set of wire snares, pegs and careful illustrated knots. The wires need resetting and inspection after actual use.

name: Covered Camping Brazier
description: A compact charcoal brazier with a wind cover and a stable folding stand. Its soot tray slides out for cleaning.

name: Cook's Traveling Roll
description: A cloth roll holding a small knife, spoon, flat scraper and nested measure. The little tools show years of sensible refinement.

name: Labeled Reagent Satchel
description: A padded satchel with snug compartments and replaceable specimen labels. Several pockets are clearly marked for empty containers.

name: Portable Copper Still
description: A compact still with well-fitted tubes and a stable stand. Its little pressure vent deserves attention rather than admiration.

name: Mechanist's Repair Roll
description: A complete roll of fine drivers, probes and gripping tools. Every recess has a small outline showing where the missing tool belongs.

name: Spring-Grip Casting Tongs
description: Long tongs with a positive spring catch and insulated handles. The jaws hold a small piece steady during a controlled working.

name: Perfumer's Traveling Case
description: A padded case of clean sample bottles, testing strips and small measures. Its lid carries a carefully made folding work surface.

name: Waterproof Courier Tube
description: A stout document tube with a screw cap and an inner waxed sleeve. Its shoulder cord has been tested with more weight than paper.

name: Silver Reservoir Pen
description: A long silver pen with a fine mana-bearing tip and an ordinary refillable ink reservoir. A small window shows when the ink is running low.

name: Living-Specimen Wardbox
description: A ventilated carrying box with adjustable padded partitions and a gentle temperature charm. Its little latch can be opened from outside only.

name: Three-Note Handler's Whistle
description: A brass whistle with three plainly marked stops. Its notes are consistent enough for a patiently trained animal to distinguish.

name: Magitech Voice Trumpet
description: A compact black voice amplifier with a silver grille and a comfortable hand strap. A small mana-fed resonator projects the speaker's actual voice.

name: Stitchkeeper's Focus Spool
description: A metal spool framing a thin mana-bearing thread. The spool turns smoothly enough to follow a measured casting gesture.

name: Long-Reach Reading Lens
description: A clear lens on a hinged arm that clamps to a table or board. Its broad focus is kind to tired eyes.

name: Nurse's Hooded Lamp
description: A carefully shaded lamp that throws a steady, warm pool of light without shining into the patient's eyes. Its handle stays cool.

name: Glassfish Lantern
description: A clear fish-shaped lantern with a little luminous bead drifting inside. The bead settles into its tail when the shutter is closed.

name: The Mapmaker's Unfolding Frame
description: A brass plotting frame with more hinged sections than fit comfortably inside its case. Every exposed scale remains perfectly aligned. It is a tool for interpreting real observations, not a map of unknown countries.

name: Mana Crystal Chips
description: A small paper packet of sorted mana-bearing crystal chips. The pieces are useful in modest fittings, repairs and experiments.

name: Clean Amber Sliver
description: A clear amber sliver wrapped in soft cloth. Its long unbroken grain makes it useful for a carefully sized magical component.

name: Coldglass Shard
description: A pale, translucent mineral shard whose surface stays cool after being held. Small flaws need checking before it is cut for a focus.

name: Prepared Wyvern Tendon
description: A treated length of tough wyvern tendon, cleaned and stretched for craft work. The wrapping records the batch and preparation date.

name: Old Dragon Scale
availability: Rare lawful dragon-gift trade; exceptional discoveries
description: A weathered fragment of naturally shed dragon scale mounted in a respectful padded case. Its surface retains a deep mineral sheen, and its provenance matters to Drakenspire buyers.

name: Sky-Silk Thread Bundle
description: A small bundle of strong, pale thread collected and prepared through established Asterveil trade. It takes dye surprisingly well.

name: Singing Basalt Core
description: A fist-sized dark stone with a narrow resonant seam. A light tap produces a clean note that fades before the next breath.

name: Crystal Moth Wing
description: A carefully preserved moth wing with fine crystalline veins. Its fragile surface scatters light into small, sharply separated bands.

name: Dewglass Resin Cake
description: A small cake of clear, mature resin cut into a lined tin. When gently warmed, its internal haze separates into fine sparkling strands.

name: Grave-Salt Packet
description: A sealed packet of dry mineral salts prepared for particular spiritual workings. Its printed label lists the batch rather than promising a cure for every haunting.

name: Sealed Storm Residue
description: A little insulated vessel containing volatile stormglass residue. Blue flickers crawl beneath the cap when it is disturbed; its brittle seal deserves careful handling.

name: Dried Mooncap Slices
description: A small jar of properly dried pale mushroom slices. The faint violet gills remain visible through the glass.

name: Key Without Teeth
description: A beautifully made brass key with a perfectly smooth blade. Its bow is worn as though someone once used it every day.

name: Bottle of Unfinished Rain
description: A stoppered bottle in which a tiny rain cloud hangs above a shallow pool. The drops stop just short of the water and begin again when the bottle is turned.

name: The Tin King of Mice
description: A palm-sized clockwork mouse wearing a crooked tin crown. Winding its key makes it march a short, determined circle.

name: Unsigned Winter Letter
description: A folded letter sealed in pale blue wax, its recipient's name rubbed away by handling. The paper carries a faint scent of pine smoke.

name: Pocket of Quiet Shell
description: A closed white shell wrapped in soft leather. Held to the ear, it carries the gentle sounds of a shore quite unlike the nearby room.

name: The Button That Never Matches
description: A handsome coat button that always seems a slightly different shade from the cloth beside it. It has an entirely ordinary sewing loop.

name: Wax Seal of the Empty House
description: An old bronze seal bearing a house with no doors. Its impressions remain crisp even when the metal feels oddly cold.

name: The Patient Paper Bird
description: A folded paper bird reinforced with fine thread. Its head bows once when placed on a warm palm, then waits without attempting to fly.

name: Pebble of Polite Disagreement
description: A smooth gray pebble that gives a soft, disapproving click when placed on another person's desk. It becomes completely silent inside a pocket.

name: The Last Unlit Lantern
description: An ornate lantern whose wick has never accepted flame. Its interior glass carries a different pattern of fine scratches on each side, as though a very patient hand once worked from within.

name: Whalebone Dice Pair
description: Two old dice with tiny carved waves in place of dots. Their edges have been rounded by use, and one carries a repaired crack.

name: Mirror of the Absent Frame
description: A small hand mirror whose reflected frame has a missing corner, although the real silver frame is complete. Turning it produces no other apparent change.

name: Field Healing Tonic
description: A small bottle of sharp-tasting red tonic. Drinking one dose restores 15 Health; the empty bottle retains an unmistakable smell of bitter berries.

name: Greater Healing Draught
description: A carefully sealed deep-red preparation. Drinking one dose restores 60 Health. Its label recommends actual treatment for the cause of a serious injury.

name: Surgical Recovery Draught
description: A strong restorative medicine in a thick amber bottle. Drinking one dose restores 100 Health, without reversing a lasting condition or bringing back the dead.

name: Stable Mana Infusion
description: A regulated blue medicine with a mineral aftertaste. Drinking one dose restores 20 Mana. Its narrow-necked bottle is sized for a single measured serving.

name: Deep Mana Infusion
description: A concentrated, regulated mana medicine with pale sediment at its base. Drinking one carefully mixed dose restores 45 Mana.

name: Azure Reserve Dose
description: An expensive mana preparation held in a dark protective vial. Drinking one dose restores 70 Mana; the lingering taste is aggressively metallic.

name: Bitter Stamina Tonic
description: A squat bottle of brown tonic that tastes worse than it smells. Drinking one dose restores 12 Stamina.

name: Trail Vigor Draught
description: A mint-scented preparation sold in a padded traveling bottle. Drinking one dose restores 24 Stamina.

name: Last-Push Dose
description: A harsh stimulant with a bright warning stripe. Drinking one dose restores 40 Stamina but costs 8 Health; it leaves the throat raw and the hands uncomfortably warm.

name: Balanced Restoration Vial
description: A small violet preparation that separates into two clear layers. Shaken and drunk as one dose, it restores 20 Health and 12 Mana.

name: Amber Recovery Gel
description: A measured edible gel in a waxed sachet. Eating one serving restores 15 Health and 10 Stamina. It tastes insistently of honey and medicinal roots.

name: Redline Tincture
description: A dangerous crimson mana stimulant sold with an unmistakable warning. Drinking one dose restores 35 Mana but costs 15 Health.

name: Smoke Pearl
description: A brittle little sphere that releases a small cloud of dense gray smoke when crushed. The smoke spreads with the actual air and makes breathing near it unpleasant.

name: Squealing Pepper Salt
description: A packet of coarse pink seasoning that whistles faintly on hot food. A carelessly thrown pinch can make a nearby nose regret the experiment.

name: Weatherproofing Wax Tin
description: A small tin of practical wax for leather and treated cloth. One careful application covers a pair of boots or a similar small article.

name: Lantern-Moss Pellet
description: A pressed pellet of prepared luminous moss. Dampening it produces a gentle green light until the little mass dries and exhausts its stored glow.

name: Footprint Dust Packet
description: A pouch of very fine pale powder that catches on fresh damp traces. It is most useful on a surface the user can actually reach and inspect.

name: Clinging Resin Bottle
description: A tightly stoppered bottle of fast-setting adhesive. Its thick stream grips well against clean, suitable surfaces and poorly against loose dirt.

name: Frostbloom Powder
description: A sealed paper twist of cold-reactive powder. Scattered on a wet patch, it produces a short-lived crust of slick frost.

name: Stinkfrog Vial
description: A little green vial with a cork tied firmly in place. Opening it releases an appalling swamp smell that clings to porous cloth.

name: Self-Warming Bun
description: A soft spiced bun wrapped in heat-holding paper. Breaking its crust releases a pleasant little puff of warmth and the smell of cinnamon.

name: Honest Blue Candy
description: A little wrapped sweet that colors the eater's tongue an impressive blue for a while. The wrapper indignantly insists that this is the intended effect.

name: Pocket Celebration
description: A paper cone of harmless colored sparks, loose streamers and a startling pop. The little fuse burns long enough for a sensible person to hold it away from their face.

name: Resin Mending Patch
description: A sealed repair patch that softens when kneaded and hardens over a clean split. It is useful for a modest emergency repair to a compatible rigid object.
